concerns.text: FR-016 and US-6 require that if N > 50, the system must 'reduce the state space size by a factor of 2' and log the effective N and state space size. Task T034 only implements logic to 'reduce N to 50' (capping the objective count) without the required state space degradation logic, leaving the spec requirement unimplemented.

FR-012 and US-4 require generating a 'held-out set of reward functions with a different noise distribution (e.g., heavy-tailed)' to satisfy Validation Independence. No task exists to implement the data generation for this specific held-out set or to execute the comparison against the theoretical bound for this non-Gaussian distribution; T045 only mentions logging deviations.

FR-010 and US-4 require a sensitivity analysis on 'at least three distinct distributions (Linear, Sparse, Non-Convex)'. The tasks only cover noise correlation (ρ) and generic non-Gaussian logging; there is no task to implement the generation or testing of the specific 'Sparse' and 'Non-Convex' reward distributions required to validate construct validity.

FR-013 and FR-014 require the system to calculate the theoretical variance of injected noise (σ²) and perform a sanity check comparing empirical noise to this known value before analysis. The tasks focus entirely on comparing the Heuristic to the Full-Batch estimate (T021a) without any task to implement the sanity check against the known ground truth σ².

SC-002 defines the 'convergence failure point' specifically as the smallest N where the sample count exceeds the bound by a factor of 1.5 AND coincides with a Pareto distance > 5%. The plan and tasks (T042, T043) replace this binary coincidence check with a Pearson/Spearman correlation coefficient; since the correlation metric does not inherently verify the specific 'factor of 1.5' threshold or the '5% distance' coincidence, the success criterion SC-002 is not fully traceable to the implemented tasks.

FR-017 requires calculating the distance to the theoretical Pareto frontier using a 'defined oracle or approximation method'. The plan mentions an 'Approximate Pareto Oracle' in src/environment/pareto_oracle.py, but the tasks (T035, T042) only reference logging the distance or using it in a correlation test without a specific task to implement or verify the oracle's approximation logic itself.

FR-006 and US-3 require performing a 'one-sample t-test' comparing the mean deviation of the heuristic's variance from the theoretical bound against zero. The tasks (T021a, T038) explicitly implement a 'Paired T-Test' (Heuristic vs. Full-Batch) and state this 'Overrides Spec FR-006'. There is no task implementing the required one-sample t-test against the theoretical bound, creating a direct gap in the validation strategy.
